atlas-us.0235: Sending a European CV: a photo, date of birth or a two-page Europass; the American résumé is one page with GPA shown.
atlas-us.0236: Treating a referral as the whole job: it raises the chance of an interview (6% of applicants, 21% of interviewees), but offers still depend on performance.
atlas-us.0237: Hiding the sponsorship question: NACE warns that saying no to hide the need could make an employer question your honesty, and recommends being up front.
atlas-us.0238: Skipping the internship: employers made full-time offers to 62% of their 2024 interns, so an internship is the main entrance, and an in-person one converts best (72%).
atlas-us.0239: American finance recruiting is in English, from the video interview to the final rounds; no certificate is asked, the interviews are the test.
atlas-us.0240: Bain’s case and behavioural interviews are conducted in English, and the cases test structured thinking and communication; no language certificate is named.
atlas-us.0241: Corporate programmes such as Deloitte’s are in English; another language is an asset in roles serving other markets but is not asked for in the pages read.
atlas-us.0242: Technical screens are in English and test coding: Bain’s technical roles use a coding challenge, and Goldman’s engineering interviews add HackerRank or CoderPad.
atlas-us.0243: Employers made full-time offers to 62% of their 2024 interns, down from two-thirds in 2023 and the lowest in five years; the 2026 report shows an average conversion rate of 63.1%.
atlas-us.0244: US recent graduates had an unemployment rate of about 5.6% in the second quarter of 2026 against 4.3% for all workers, and 42% were underemployed.
atlas-us.0245: For internationals the outcomes are worse: post-graduation employment is 44.6% against 62.1% for domestic students, at an average starting salary of $80,785 driven by STEM fields; Duke’s master’s graduates needing a visa had a 71% offer rate at six months against 85% with work rights.
atlas-us.0247: A SEVP-certified school issues the I-20, which states the money you must show; there is no federal threshold. Pay the SEVIS fee before an in-person interview, with social-media profiles set to public.
atlas-us.0248: The visa can be issued up to 365 days before the course and you may arrive up to 30 days before it starts. On campus you may work 20 hours a week in term.
atlas-us.0249: An F-1 visa for Italians is valid 16 months, for British citizens 60: your status continues, but re-entering after a trip abroad may need a new visa.
atlas-us.0252: Through a sponsor designated by the State Department. Intern: enrolled abroad or graduated within 12 months, up to 12 months. Trainee: a degree and a year of experience abroad, or five years of experience, up to 18 months.
atlas-us.0253: Inside a US degree, curricular practical training has since August 2026 been allowed only where the course requires it of every student.
atlas-us.0255: at least $100,000 per accident or illness
atlas-us.0257: Only after a US degree: up to 12 months of work in your field, with 90 days of unemployment allowed. A degree on the DHS STEM list adds 24 months with an E-Verify employer.
atlas-us.0258: Apply from 90 days before to 60 days after the programme ends, within 30 days of the school’s recommendation.
atlas-us.0260: STEM status follows the programme’s CIP code, not its name: Finance (52.0801) is not on the list.
atlas-us.0261: 65,000 visas a year plus 20,000 for US master’s degrees; a European master’s does not count. Since 2026 the lottery is weighted by wage level, and universities are outside the cap.
atlas-us.0262: A $100,000 payment set by proclamation runs to 21 September 2027, but two courts have struck down its rules and it is not being collected for now.
atlas-us.0263: Projected odds per person, lowest to highest wage level
atlas-us.0266: L-1 moves you within your company after a year with it abroad in the last three. E-1 and E-2 serve trade and investment for treaty countries, Italy and the UK among them; the employee must share the company’s nationality. O-1 is for extraordinary ability.
atlas-us.0268: $205 for L and O, $315 for E
atlas-us.0270: A J-1 Research Scholar stays up to five years, a Short-term Scholar six months; a PhD is usually an F-1 with assistantships counted as campus work.
atlas-us.0271: Students and scholars on F or J are exempt from Social Security and Medicare for their first five calendar years.
atlas-us.0273: Some J-1 holders must live two years at home before an H or L visa or a green card.
atlas-us.0275: There is no working-holiday visa. The nearest is Summer Work Travel: full-time students enrolled abroad, up to four months in the break between academic years, with seasonal work arranged by a sponsor.
atlas-us.0278: Citizens of 24 EU countries, and British citizens with the right of abode, visit up to 90 days with an ESTA: no work and no study for credit. Bulgaria, Cyprus and Romania are outside the programme and need a B visa.
atlas-us.0279: An ESTA entry cannot be changed into another status inside the US.
atlas-us.0282: Get the I-20 (F or M student) or DS-2019 (J exchange) from a certified school or sponsor, with name and birth date exactly as in your passport, then pay the SEVIS I-901 fee (F/M $350, J $220) before the interview.
atlas-us.0283: Fill in the DS-160, pay the visa fee ($185 for F, M, J and B; $205 for H, L and O) and book the interview through usvisa-info in your country of citizenship or residence. Set your social media profiles to public, and travel with a passport valid 6 months beyond your return.
atlas-us.0284: Students may get the visa up to 365 days ahead but arrive no more than 30 days before the programme starts.
atlas-us.0285: Report every change of address to USCIS on form AR-11 within 10 days.
atlas-us.0286: At the border show your I-20 or DS-2019, passport and proof of funds; your arrival record (I-94) is electronic. If documents are missing you get form I-515A and 30 days to fix it.
atlas-us.0287: Check in with your school’s designated official (DSO) as soon as you arrive, and before the programme start date.
atlas-us.0288: A Social Security number is only for people authorised to work (on campus, CPT, OPT): apply online, then in person at a Social Security office at least 10 days after arriving, with letters from your DSO and employer. It is free and the card comes by post in 5 to 10 working days.
atlas-us.0289: Without one, use an ITIN (form W-7) for tax. File form 8843 every year, and form 1040-NR if you have taxable US income.
atlas-us.0290: J exchange visitors must hold insurance of at least $100,000 per incident, $25,000 for repatriation and $50,000 for evacuation. For F-1 students no federal rule requires insurance: ask your school what it requires.
atlas-us.0291: Keep your status: study full time, do no unauthorised work, and extend before your end date. To travel, get your DSO’s signature on the I-20 within the last year and stay away no more than 5 months.
atlas-us.0292: After finishing your programme you have a 60-day grace period today; a pending rule would change it to 30 days.
atlas-us.0293: Moving from F-1 to H-1B inside the US escapes the $100,000 payment only if the change is granted: not if it is refused or you leave before the decision.
atlas-us.0294: Doing something your visa forbids within 90 days of entry, such as working on a visitor visa, lets the consul presume you lied when applying.
atlas-us.0295: Apply for an ESTA only on esta.cbp.dhs.gov; dual citizens of Cuba, Iran, Iraq, North Korea, Sudan or Syria, and recent visitors to several of those countries, need a visa.
atlas-us.0296: Messages saying you won the green-card lottery and asking for money are scams: the State Department runs it.
atlas-us.0297: A rule ending “duration of status” for students, with four-year admissions and a 30-day grace period, is postponed by a court; today the 60-day grace period still applies.
atlas-us.0298: Universities sued on 5 October 2026 over the narrower curricular-training rules.
atlas-us.0299: Appeals on the $100,000 H-1B payment, and a separate proposed $103,265 fee on capped petitions.
atlas-us.0300: A rule on OPT fees has cleared White House review but is unpublished; the amount is unknown.
atlas-us.0301: A $250 visa integrity fee is in the law, but no one has confirmed it is being collected.
atlas-us.0302: No diversity-lottery visas have been issued since 31 August 2026.
